propositions: The rebar project's concurrency-heavy workload (multi-process writers, file locks, detached children) causes trigger over-fire: committed high-precision tier fires on 13.3% of diffs, noisy tier adds 22.0% more, for 35.3% combined, with three traced corpus bugs triggering only through noisy-tier vocabulary.

Project overlay mechanism does not yet document the two-layer trigger design (committed high-precision tier vs. project-specific noisy tier) or provide worked examples for other projects to replicate.

The code_review.concurrency project entry in .rebar/criteria_routing.json must add project-specific trigger tokens (.lock, retry, Popen, setsid, fork, stage_and_commit, push_tickets_branch, refs/reconciler/) and file globs to enable reproduction of load-bearing corpus bug triggers.
Config-effect test must verify that diffs containing project-only tokens (e.g., index.lock) fire the concurrency overlay under this repo's effective routing but not under committed-only routing.
